title: Cure Mailing Allowance — Hardship and Protective Holds
content:
Under Hardship and Protective Holds, a cure notice adds a cure mailing allowance to the days allowed to cure, once, according to how the documentation submissions on the hold request have arrived.

| How the submissions on the request have arrived | Cure mailing allowance |
|---|---|
| At least one by mail or fax, and none by the online portal or email | 7 calendar days (paper mailing allowance) |
| At least one by mail or fax, and at least one by the online portal or email | 3 calendar days (mixed mailing allowance) |
| Otherwise (none by mail or fax) | None |

**Basis.** The test counts every documentation submission received on the request, of any kind, by the channel recorded for it. Mail and fax form the paper group; the online portal and email form the electronic group. A submission recorded as arriving by phone belongs to neither group.

## Combinations

| Paper-group submissions | Electronic-group submissions | Allowance |
|---|---|---|
| 1 or more | 0 | 7 days |
| 1 or more | 1 or more | 3 days |
| 0 | 1 or more | None |
| 0 | 0 | None |

## Examples (hypothetical)

- Two submissions, one by mail and one by fax: paper only, 7 days are added.
- One submission by fax and a later one through the online portal: mixed, 3 days are added.
- Two submissions by email: no paper submission, nothing is added.
